name: Productivity Coach Demo | Task Status Sync

parameters.content:
## Productivity Coach Demo | Task Status Sync

Keeps parent and child statuses consistent across Weekly Plan → Tasks → Subtasks. No AI: fixed rules only.
Runs every 12 hours (catches ticks made by hand in Notion), and is also called by "Productivity Coach Demo | Productivity Agent" right after each reply (so Telegram changes cascade at once).
Standalone-capable: yes (own schedule). All runs (success and failure) are saved to the execution list, so a sync can be verified without inspecting Notion or workflow static data.

## Status Sync

Triggered by: Every 12 hours or Receive Sync Call (from the "Productivity Agent").

1. Reads all rows of Weekly Plan, Tasks and Subtasks.
2. Down: a Done/Cancelled parent closes its open children the same way.
3. Up: when all children are closed (at least one Done), the parent becomes Done.
4. The most recent edit wins, so reopening one item by hand is not undone.
5. Writes only the statuses that changed.

## Due Date Sync (Compute Due Date Changes)

6. Compares every item's Due Date to what was seen on the previous sweep (kept in this workflow's own static data, not a Notion column) -- catches a date changed by the agent, by hand in Notion, or by any other route. A brand-new item's date is only recorded as a baseline, never counted as a move.
7. If a Task's date changed, its open Subtasks are forced onto the same new date and counted as moved too -- Subtasks never had their own date-tracking before this.
8. Any item whose date changed gets Times Moved bumped by 1 (Weekly Plan, Tasks and Subtasks all have this column). The "Productivity Agent" no longer bumps this itself during the Sunday close-out -- this sweep is now the single source of truth, so it can't be double-counted.
